name: Oil & Gas
one_liner: Finding, producing, moving and refining hydrocarbons, a capital-heavy commodity business whose profits swing with oil and gas prices.
how_it_makes_money: Upstream producers sell crude oil and natural gas at market prices, so earnings track commodity prices minus lifting and development costs. Midstream companies earn largely fee-based, volume-driven tolls on pipelines, storage and processing. Downstream refiners earn the crack spread between crude input costs and product prices, and marketers add retail fuel margins.
revenue_formula: Upstream revenue = production volume (boe/day) × days × realized price per boe
Refining gross margin = throughput (bbl/day) × utilization × crack spread
Midstream revenue = contracted/throughput volume × tariff per unit
cost_structure: Capex (drilling, completions, facilities): the dominant spend; sustaining capex needed just to offset decline
Lease operating / lifting costs: per-barrel cost to keep wells producing
Royalties and production taxes: paid to landowners and governments as a share of revenue
Crude feedstock: the largest cost for refiners, typically the vast majority of refinery costs
Depreciation, depletion and amortization: large non-cash charge on capitalized reserves
Transportation and gathering fees: cost to move barrels to market
margins: Highly cyclical: upstream margins can swing from losses to very high returns across the price cycle, while midstream is steadier and refining depends on crack spreads. The spread is driven by breakeven cost per barrel, asset quality and capital discipline.

key_metrics.name: Barrels of oil equivalent per day (boe/d)
key_metrics.what: Production volume, the core output measure for upstream companies.

key_metrics.name: Breakeven price ($/bbl)
key_metrics.what: The oil price needed to cover costs and capex; low-breakeven assets survive downturns.

key_metrics.name: Lifting cost ($/boe)
key_metrics.what: Operating cost to produce each barrel, a key efficiency benchmark.

key_metrics.name: Reserve replacement ratio (RRR)
key_metrics.what: New reserves added versus production; below 100% means the reserve base is shrinking.

key_metrics.name: Crack spread
key_metrics.what: Difference between refined product prices and crude cost, the main refining margin driver.

key_metrics.name: Refinery utilization
key_metrics.what: Share of refining capacity in use, which drives fixed-cost absorption.

key_metrics.name: Decline rate
key_metrics.what: How fast output from existing wells falls, especially steep for shale.

trends: Capital discipline and shareholder returns (buybacks, dividends) prioritized over volume growth
Consolidation in US shale as large players buy acreage and scale
LNG export build-out linking US gas to global markets
Methane reduction, emissions targets and carbon capture as license-to-operate issues
Majors balancing oil and gas cash flows against low-carbon investments
Geopolitics and OPEC+ supply decisions driving price volatility
